- As announced in the 1.86 release notes, the deprecated XMSS / XMSS^MT implementation under org.bouncycastle.pqc.crypto.xmss has been removed, together with its key handling in the org.bouncycastle.pqc.crypto.util PublicKeyFactory, PrivateKeyFactory, SubjectPublicKeyInfoFactory and PrivateKeyInfoFactory. Use the implementation promoted in 1.86 instead - key parameters in org.bouncycastle.crypto.params, XMSSKeyPairGenerator and XMSSMTKeyPairGenerator in org.bouncycastle.crypto.generators, XMSSSigner and XMSSMTSigner in org.bouncycastle.crypto.signers, and the org.bouncycastle.crypto.util key factories. Keys written by the removed package, including those carrying its Java-serialized BDS state, are read by the promoted classes. The deprecated JCE classes under org.bouncycastle.pqc.jcajce are unaffected, as they already use the promoted implementation.

+- The Classic McEliece implementation (ISO/IEC 18033-2:2006/Amd 2:2026, Clause 13) is now deprecated, as it is now believed unsafe to use, and will be removed in a future release: CMCEKeyPairGenerator, CMCEKEMGenerator and CMCEKEMExtractor, the CMCE key parameter classes in org.bouncycastle.crypto.params, the org.bouncycastle.crypto.kems.cmce engine package, CMCEParameterSpec, the CMCEKey, CMCEPublicKey and CMCEPrivateKey interfaces in org.bouncycastle.jcajce.interfaces, and the BC provider classes under org.bouncycastle.jcajce.provider.asymmetric.cmce. The provider registrations are unchanged.

- As flagged in the 1.86 release notes, org.bouncycastle.operator.jcajce.JcaContentVerifierProviderBuilder no longer verifies legacy generic composite (id_alg_composite) signatures, whose creation was removed in 1.86: a ContentVerifierProvider from it now refuses the id_alg_composite algorithm with an OperatorCreationException, whatever key it was built with. The BC provider's X509Certificate.verify() and X509CRL.verify() likewise now throw NoSuchAlgorithmException for an id_alg_composite signature rather than checking it. Modern fixed-algorithm Composite ML-DSA signatures are unaffected, as is verifying an ordinary signature with one component of a legacy CompositePublicKey.

- ParametersWithUKM now nests outside ParametersWithRandom in the light-weight API, alongside ParametersWithContext and ParametersWithID, as the org.bouncycastle.crypto.params package documentation now describes. GOST28147WrapEngine, CryptoProWrapEngine and ECVKOAgreement accept ParametersWithUKM(ParametersWithRandom(key)); the two wrap engines also still accept the earlier ParametersWithRandom(ParametersWithUKM(key)), and the provider's GOST 28147 key wrap ciphers now build the new form. A ParametersWithUKM with no random inside is unaffected.
